abstract:
BACKGROUND AND OBJECTIVE: Pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma (PDAC) remains one of the gastrointestinal malignancies least amenable to durable therapeutic control. Resistance is generated by the intrinsic aggressiveness of the malignant epithelium and is reinforced by a compact desmoplastic microenvironment in which extracellular matrix (ECM) accumulation, vascular compression, impaired perfusion, and immune exclusion are closely interlocked. The limited clinical yield of nonselective stromal-depleting strategies has sharpened interest in localized, controllable, and context-sensitive stromal remodeling. This narrative review synthesizes the biological rationale, mechanistic routes, therapeutic implications, and translational limits of engineered bacteria-mediated stromal remodeling in PDAC.
METHODS: PubMed, Web of Science, and Scopus were searched from database inception to 30 April 2026 using Medical Subject Headings (MeSH) and free-text terms related to PDAC, engineered bacteria, bacterial cancer therapy, tumor stroma, ECM remodeling, hyaluronan, collagen, drug delivery, immune sensitization, and clinical translation. A targeted update of PubMed and a cross-registry search of ClinicalTrials.gov and the World Health Organization International Clinical Trials Registry Platform (WHO ICTRP) were performed on 24 July 2026. English-language full-text literature was prioritized, and PDAC-specific evidence was distinguished from broader bacteria-based oncology evidence.
KEY CONTENT AND FINDINGS: Engineered bacterial systems are appealing living therapeutic platforms because tumor tropism, preferential residence in hypoxic or necrotic tumor territories, and programmable local payload release can be assembled within a single biological chassis. In PDAC models, bacteria-mediated stromal remodeling has been investigated through hyaluronan degradation, collagen depletion, dual ECM co-depletion, and indirect modulation of pancreatic stellate cell (PSC)/cancer-associated fibroblast-associated fibrotic programs. These approaches may improve intratumoral drug penetration, mitigate pressure-related transport barriers, increase immune-cell access, and support multimodal local therapy. The evidential base, however, remains predominantly preclinical; direct clinical validation in PDAC is still limited.
CONCLUSIONS: At present, engineered bacteria should be interpreted primarily as local stromal-opening and delivery-enabling platforms, not as clinically established therapies for PDAC. Their translational value will depend on whether stromal remodeling can be delivered safely, reproducibly, and in a manner that is measurable in patients.
key_points_ko: 유전자 재조합 세균은 종양 친화성과 저산소 구역 농축 특성을 이용해 췌장암 기질 개방 및 약물 전달을 도울 수 있는 플랫폼입니다.
전임상 모델에서 히알루론산 분해, 콜라겐 감소, 췌장별상세포(PSC) 조절을 통해 항암제 침투력과 면역세포 접근성을 향상시켰습니다.
현재 췌장암 환자를 대상으로 한 직접적인 임상 검증은 제한적이며 실제 환자에서의 안전성과 재현성 확보가 향후 과제입니다.
summary_ko: 본 논문은 췌장관선암(PDAC)의 종양 기질을 개방하기 위한 유전자 재조합 세균(engineered bacteria) 치료 플랫폼의 가능성과 한계를 종합한 서술적 종설 논문입니다. 췌장암은 치밀한 결합조직 형성성 기질로 인해 약물 전달과 면역세포 침투가 극도로 제한됩니다. 연구진은 저산소 종양 부위로 이동하는 세균 특성을 활용해 히알루론산 분해 및 콜라겐 감소 등의 기질 리모델링 효과를 분석했습니다. 유전자 재조합 세균은 약물 침투를 돕는局所(국소) 플랫폼으로 기대받고 있으나 현재까지의 연구 근거는 대부분 전임상 단계에 머물러 있습니다.
title: Engineered bacteria-mediated stromal remodeling in pancreatic ductal adenocarcinoma: therapeutic opportunities and translational limits-a narrative review
title_ko: 췌장관선암에서 유전자 재조합 세균 매개 기질 리모델링: 치료적 기회와 임상적 적용의 한계에 대한 서술적 검토
